root_cause: The dominant failure signature is that the FIFO's status flags do not track the occupancy count as required by the specification: full stays 0 when the FIFO is full (@85 ns), empty stays 1 when data is present (@125 ns), and almost_full stays 0 when the AF_LEVEL threshold is crossed (@210 ns). These stale/late flags then cause the downstream protocol violations (write when full @355 ns, read when empty @420 ns) and the simultaneous read/write data mismatch @350 ns. Structural RTL analysis confirms a reset-coverage defect: 'fifo_count' is written in the sequential block at projects/fifo/rtl/sync_fifo.sv:63 but is not assigned in the reset clause, so occupancy (and hence every flag derived from it) starts from an indeterminate/uninitialized value and remains permanently skewed relative to the actual pointer difference (rd_ptr/wr_ptr are reset at line 43). This is a violation of REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-011 and REQ-012 by the design → Decision Rule Case 6/7/8 (RTL violates spec, uninitialized state, protocol protection not implemented correctly).
category: Functional / Reset Initialization → Status-Flag & Protocol Violation
spec_reference: REQ-007 (full), REQ-008 (empty), REQ-009 (almost_full/AF_LEVEL), REQ-011 (overflow), REQ-012 (underflow), REQ-013 (wr_count); Reset Behavior section: 'reset (low, asynchronous) resets ...'
log_reference: @85 ns Full flag mismatch (exp 1, got 0); @125 ns Empty flag mismatch (exp 0, got 1); @210 ns Almost full flag mismatch (exp 1, got 0); @350 ns data mismatch on simultaneous rd/wr; @355 ns write while full; @420 ns read while empty

evidence.description: Sequential block drives fifo_count and all status flags but fifo_count is absent from the reset clause, leaving occupancy uninitialized after reset (Case 7 style X/indeterminate state).
evidence.snippet: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin if (!rst_n) begin full<=0; empty<=1; ... /* fifo_count NOT reset */ end else ... end

evidence.description: wr_ptr/rd_ptr ARE reset, so pointer-based occupancy and the separately maintained fifo_count can diverge immediately after reset, producing permanently wrong flags.

Three independent flag checks (full, empty, almost_full) all fail in the same direction: the flag lags/does not reflect actual occupancy — a systematic count/threshold defect, not a random data corruption.

Overflow (write when full) and underflow (read when empty) protection failed, i.e. REQ-011/REQ-012 protection mechanisms are ineffective because they depend on the broken full/empty flags → Case 8 protocol implemented incorrectly in RTL.

Spec unambiguously requires full when no space remains, empty when no data available, almost_full at AF_LEVEL, and one-cycle overflow/underflow pulses. No self-contradiction exists in the requirement set, so Case 9 (Spec Bug) is excluded.
Concurrent read/write handling corrupts dout/count bookkeeping — a classic symptom of incorrect count update for the simultaneous case in the same block at line 63.

evidence.description: TB predictor source unavailable, so a scoreboard off-by-one cannot be fully excluded; the '@85 ns Expected 15, Got 15' message is the only TB-side anomaly and affects a single check, not the flag failures.

reasoning.observation: Seven errors: three status-flag mismatches, one data mismatch on simultaneous rd/wr, and two protocol-protection violations (write-when-full, read-when-empty).
reasoning.inference: Failures cluster around occupancy tracking and flag generation rather than data path storage.

reasoning.observation: Spec REQ-007..REQ-013 define full/empty/almost_full/almost_empty/overflow/underflow/count behavior consistently; no contradictory statements.
RTL structural analysis: fifo_count is written in the always block at line 63 but is missing from that block's reset clause; pointers at line 43 are reset.
reasoning.inference: Post-reset occupancy is indeterminate; all flags derived from fifo_count are wrong from time 0 — an RTL initialization defect (Case 7) and a spec violation (Case 6).

reasoning.observation: full=0 at the moment the scoreboard expects full=1, and empty=1 when data should be readable; almost_full never asserts at threshold.
reasoning.inference: Flags are computed from a stale/registered count instead of the next-state count, so threshold crossings are missed or delayed — consistent with the reset/count defect.

reasoning.observation: Overflow/underflow guard errors occur AFTER the flag errors (355 ns, 420 ns).
reasoning.inference: Protocol violations are downstream consequences of the broken flags, confirming a single RTL root cause (Case 8) rather than bad stimulus; a driver bug would not also corrupt full/empty flag values reported by the DUT.

reasoning.observation: One log line reports 'FIFO count mismatch: Expected 15, Got 15' where expected == actual, and scoreboard source was not collected.
reasoning.inference: There is a secondary TB reporting/compare defect worth fixing, but it does not explain the DUT flag values; it lowers confidence modestly rather than changing the classification.

reasoning.observation: Driver and monitor artifacts show no reported protocol/sampling anomalies, and deterministic pre-analysis independently suggests RTL Bug with a reset-coverage finding.
reasoning.inference: Cases 1–5 (TB Bug paths) are not supported by evidence; final classification is RTL Bug.

recommended_fixes.action: 1) In the reset branch of the always block at sync_fifo.sv:63, initialize fifo_count <= '0 (along with full, empty, almost_full, almost_empty, overflow, underflow) so occupancy is deterministic after the asynchronous active-low reset. 2) Derive full/empty/almost_full/almost_empty from the next-state count (fifo_count_next computed from wr_en & ~full and rd_en & ~empty in the same cycle) or make them combinational functions of fifo_count so they assert on the cycle the threshold is reached rather than one cycle late. 3) Ensure the simultaneous read/write case keeps fifo_count unchanged while still forwarding/advancing both pointers, which fixes the @350 ns data mismatch. 4) Gate the write/read strobes with the corrected full/empty flags and pulse overflow/underflow for exactly one cycle per REQ-011/REQ-012. 5) Separately, audit the scoreboard count-compare that reported 'Expected 15, Got 15' (likely wrong field printed or wrong operator) — this is a TB reporting issue layered on top of the RTL defect.
